A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BayesVLM/ProbCosine research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including v5's added Sections F.11–F.13.

before.justification: v4 reports original zero-shot classification, calibration, active-learning, runtime, and sensitivity results in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds proxy-corruption experiments, distribution-shift evaluations, and a cross-modal curvature analysis.

M1.justification: The modality-wise Laplace approximation, KFAC-GGN posterior estimation, ProbCosine prediction, and active-learning procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. The empirical Fisher introduced in F.13 is an assessment tool, not a replacement for the proposed posterior-estimation method.

E1.justification: Coverage expands within image classification through ImageNet-A and controlled grayscale, JPEG-compression, and blur shifts of the LAION proxy data. ImageNet-Sketch was already evaluated in active learning; v5 additionally reports zero-shot results on it. Existing datasets and tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in existing experiments is unchanged, including the PCME++ and ProLIP comparisons. New Table 17 reuses CLIP, temperature scaling, and Farina et al.'s TTA from the existing zero-shot comparator set.

E3.justification: F.11 introduces controlled experiments with six severity levels for each of three proxy-data corruptions, estimating Hessians on corrupted data while evaluating clean benchmarks. F.12 adds zero-shot shift evaluations, and F.13 introduces a curvature-ratio diagnostic using 50k and 100k sampled gradient components. Previously reported experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Sections F.11–F.13 test sensitivity to proxy-data degradation, calibration under severe test-distribution shifts, and the magnitude of cross-modal curvature omitted by the independence approximation. These substantially expand robustness and assumption checks. The qualitative corruption example displayed in v5's main text already existed in v4's Appendix F.6.

E5.justification: F.13 adds Monte Carlo curvature estimation across three random seeds, with ± values in Table 18; the specific dispersion statistic is not identified there. Existing standard-error reporting, paired t-tests, and five- or ten-trial sensitivity studies are unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and plotted results are retained, while Tables 14–18 add substantive findings. Under increasing proxy blur, FOOD-101 ECE rises from 1.69 to 11.52. Table 17 reports BayesVLM ECE of 0.23 on ImageNet-A versus temperature scaling's 0.18, and 0.08 on ImageNet-Sketch versus 0.13. Table 18 adds curvature ratios of 0.363±0.002 and 0.374±0.035.

T1.justification: F.13 adds the mathematical definition of a cross-modal curvature ratio in Equation 116 and an empirical-Fisher approximation for estimating it. The existing likelihood, Laplace, ProbCosine, and online-update derivations are unchanged; the independence assumption itself was already present.

C1.justification: The abstract and listed contributions retain their original claims. Section 5 modestly broadens claimed applicability to OOD/failure detection and uncertainty-aware retrieval, presenting these as prospective applications without new evaluations.

C2.justification: v5 qualifies proxy robustness by distinguishing mild stylistic changes from corruption that destroys semantic information. It explicitly lists projection-parameter independence as a limitation and interprets the new curvature diagnostic as support for that approximation. F.12 also attributes TTA's accuracy advantages to crop coverage.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement adds access information for models and precomputed Hessian estimates alongside the retained code link. New analyses document corruption parameter grids, curvature sampling details, and 64-crop TTA. Existing implementation and training details are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and dedicated related-work sections are unchanged. F.12 adds limited comparative positioning by explicitly describing BayesVLM as complementary to TTA and suggesting their combination for accuracy and uncertainty benefits.

P1.justification: Section 5 becomes Discussion & Conclusion with added application and limitation discussion. Section 4.3 brings forward an existing appendix explanation, and Appendix F gains three subsections. Affiliation, acknowledgement, and header text receive limited edits; the overall narrative and derivation structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 substantially extends the visual evidence with corruption-sweep tables, an augmentation image grid, and new benchmark and curvature tables (Tables 14–18, Figure 17). v4's Figure 11 is reproduced as main-text Figure 5 while retained as appendix Figure 12. Existing displays largely persist, and Table 1 corrects the NLPD direction arrow.

improvement.justification: Compared with v4's proxy-dataset comparison and qualitative corruption example, v5's controlled tests expose a useful calibration failure boundary under severe blur and strengthen evidence about distribution shifts. Explicit limitations and model/Hessian access information also help. These are bounded gains: the independence diagnostic uses an empirical-Fisher proxy, and the new OOD/retrieval applications remain untested.
